clue.text: Throw a dollar

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to throw off a rider, as a bronco does
second meaning: American slang for a dollar

explanation.walkthrough: Read as one instruction it sounds like tossing a coin; the two parts are separate senses of one word. Pearl Buck won the Nobel Prize in Literature.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse that bucks hurls its rider off, and a buck is everyday American slang for a single banknote.

clue.text: Shout with alarm, "That hurts!"

parts.note: an alarm bell
ow is the cry of pain

explanation.surface: Someone yells in fright: that's painful!
explanation.walkthrough: Saul Bellow won the Nobel Prize in Literature.
explanation.definitionFit: To bellow is to roar or call out loudly, a forceful kind of yelling.

clue.text: Publisher's canto ends uproariously

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: in an uproar things are thrown into chaos, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: the two words are taken as written for their letters

explanation.surface: A publisher whose verse sections close in a riot of noise.
explanation.definitionFit: Condé Nast is the American magazine house behind Vogue and The New Yorker.

clue.text: Apostle, for the most part good and crazy, is censorious

indicators.note: only most of the apostle's name is used, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: Jude is one of the twelve apostles
mental is informal for mad

explanation.surface: A disciple who is mostly virtuous but unhinged turns out to be fault-finding.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone censorious is quick to criticise others, which is what a judgmental person does.

clue.text: Frank's guru and mystic: Ed

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is'; frank means open, unguarded

indicators.note: mystic suggests something obscure and puzzling, so the letters are mystified into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Frank's spiritual teacher, an occult figure named Ed.
explanation.walkthrough: Frank looks like a person's name; it is the adjective meaning candid.
explanation.definitionFit: Frank speech is candid and open, with no caution held back, which is what unguarded remarks are.

clue.text: Ganja stashed in Integra's seats

indicators.note: something stashed is concealed, here inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the car's name and the start of the next word

explanation.surface: Cannabis smuggled under the seats of a Honda Integra.
explanation.walkthrough: Günter Grass won the Nobel Prize in Literature.
explanation.definitionFit: Ganja is a name for cannabis, and grass is a slang term for the same drug.

clue.text: One that provides goal to borrower

parts.note: an end is an aim
one who owes money

explanation.surface: A lender who gives a borrower something to aim for.
explanation.definitionFit: An endower provides a fund or gift, endowing an institution with income.

clue.text: Kill insect swallowing sodium

indicators.note: the insect takes the element inside it

parts.note: the termite is a wood-eating insect

explanation.surface: Exterminate a bug that has eaten some salt.
explanation.definitionFit: To terminate is to end something, and in thriller slang to murder someone.

clue.text: Possible murder weapon tossed into lake (loch) with negligence

indicators.note: the weapon is thrown into the water words and ends up between them

parts.note: Loch Ness is the famous Scottish lake
an ax, the American spelling of axe

explanation.surface: A careless killer throws the weapon into a Scottish loch.
explanation.walkthrough: Halldór Laxness, the Icelandic novelist, won the Nobel Prize in Literature.
explanation.definitionFit: Laxness is slackness or carelessness, a failure to take proper care.

clue.text: Cerf edited article within The Nation

indicators.note: the article sits inside the rearranged letters
an editor rearranges copy, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written: the surname of the publisher Bennett Cerf

explanation.surface: Bennett Cerf, the Random House publisher, edits an article inside this very magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: Anatole France won the Nobel Prize in Literature.
explanation.definitionFit: France is a European country, and nation is a synonym for country.

clue.text: Ship's protective interior

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a large passenger ship; the 's stands for 'is', joining the two halves
second meaning: a lining fitted inside something to protect it

explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe s looks possessive, as if the protective interior belongs to a ship; it is really 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: An ocean liner is a passenger vessel, and a liner is also an inner layer guarding something, like a bin liner.

clue.text: $1,000 photos containing leader of rowing competition

parts.note: a grand is slang for a thousand dollars

indicators.note: the photos word holds the next letter inside it

parts.note: pix is informal for pictures

indicators.note: the first letter of rowing leads that word

parts.note: only its first letter is used

explanation.surface: A thousand dollars' worth of pictures from a rowing regatta.
explanation.definitionFit: A Grand Prix is a major race or contest, especially in motor sport, so it is a kind of competition.

clue.text: McKellen and Fleming going after busted canoe with people from Vanuatu, for example

indicators.note: the actors' first names come after the rearranged boat
a busted canoe is broken up, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
Ian McKellen the actor and Ian Fleming the novelist: two Ians

explanation.surface: Two famous Ians follow a wrecked canoe among South Pacific islanders.
explanation.definitionFit: Vanuatu is a Pacific island nation in Oceania, so its inhabitants are among the region's peoples.

clue.text: Chalky isle in the sound

indicators.note: heard aloud, the island's name matches the answer; a sound is also a strait, which disguises the signal

parts.note: the Isle of Wight lies off England's south coast

explanation.surface: A chalk island sitting in a sea channel, as the Isle of Wight does in the Solent.
explanation.walkthrough: Patrick White, the Australian novelist, won the Nobel Prize in Literature.
explanation.definitionFit: Chalk is pale, so something chalky has the colour of chalk, a pale near-colourless shade.

clue.text: New Delhi's defense

indicators.note: new makes the letters into a fresh arrangement, disguised as part of the city name

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: India's capital and its military protection.
explanation.walkthrough: New Delhi reads as a single place name; New is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A shield is a protective barrier, so it serves as a guard against attack.

clue.text: Vintage transportation for red wine that sounds attractive

indicators.note: the word is only heard, so a different spelling enters the grid

parts.note: handsome means good-looking
cab is short for cabernet sauvignon

explanation.surface: Old-fashioned transport carrying a red wine that seems appealing.
explanation.definitionFit: The hansom cab was a two-wheeled horse-drawn carriage for hire in the nineteenth century, an antique conveyance.

clue.text: Disrupt raids on ancient people

indicators.note: disrupting the words breaks their letters apart and reorders them

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Breaking up raids by some old tribe.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dorians were one of the Greek tribes of antiquity, settling the Peloponnese and Crete.

clue.text: Famous Cuban brought up reactionary fascist, practically

indicators.note: reacting means acting back, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: a child brought up is raised

indicators.note: practically means almost, so the last letter is left off

parts.note: a Nazi

explanation.surface: A Cuban celebrity raised as an almost-fascist reactionary.
explanation.definitionFit: Desi Arnaz was the Cuban-born bandleader and actor who starred in I Love Lucy.

clue.text: Suffering a reverse, went into the hole with editor in blue jeans

indicators.note: a reverse is a setback, but here it turns the word backwards

parts.note: mined, as a miner digs a hole

explanation.surface: A miner who had a setback, then dug in denim beside an editor.
explanation.definitionFit: Denim is the cotton twill used for jeans, so someone wearing jeans is clothed in it.

clue.text: Hoffman hiding black trashcan

indicators.note: the actor's name conceals the letter inside it

parts.note: Dustin Hoffman, the actor

explanation.surface: An actor concealing a dark rubbish bin.
explanation.definitionFit: Dustbin is the British word for a garbage can, the container for household refuse.

clue.text: Strong wind, with fog and a bit of rain, over Alabama

indicators.note: in a down entry, one piece sits over the next

parts.note: mist is light fog

indicators.note: just one bit, the first letter, of rain

parts.note: only its first letter is used
AL is the postal code for Alabama

explanation.surface: A gale with fog and a shower blowing over Alabama.
explanation.walkthrough: Gabriela Mistral, the Chilean poet, won the Nobel Prize in Literature.
explanation.definitionFit: The mistral is a cold north wind that blows down the Rhône valley into southern France.

clue.text: Vocalist that's red-hot?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a person who sings
second meaning, whimsical: something red-hot scorches, so it is a singe-er

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the made-up second sense. Isaac Bashevis Singer won the Nobel Prize in Literature.
explanation.definitionFit: A vocalist performs songs; the second reading treats the word as an agent noun from scorching lightly.

clue.text: Voiced contrary opinions in barnyard language?

indicators.note: spoken out loud, so the sound matters rather than the spelling

parts.note: nays are votes against

explanation.surface: Dissent expressed in animal noises, as if a farmyard took a vote.
explanation.definitionFit: Horses neigh, so the noises a horse makes are its farmyard speech.

clue.text: Forceful company man

parts.note: a gent is a gentleman

explanation.surface: A firm's employee with a powerful manner.
explanation.definitionFit: A cogent argument is compelling and persuasive, carrying real force.

clue.text: Maximum invested in Social Security checks

indicators.note: money invested in a fund goes inside it, so this word goes inside the other

parts.note: SS is the US abbreviation for Social Security
the top is the highest level

explanation.surface: The most money paid into the pension programme produces the cheques.
explanation.definitionFit: To check something is to halt it, and a stop is a halt, so these are verbs of restraint.

clue.text: He had a hunch involving somewhat tragic doom

parts.note: quasi means seemingly or partly

indicators.note: a tragic fate is one that has gone wrong, so the letters are disordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A man with a hunch about a tragic fate.
explanation.walkthrough: A hunch here is a hump: Victor Hugo's hunchback of Notre-Dame. Salvatore Quasimodo, the Italian poet, was a Nobel laureate.
explanation.definitionFit: The bell-ringer in Hugo's novel has a hunched back, so the definition is a playful description of the character.

clue.text: Question and answer to dishonor Arab country

parts.note: to tar someone is to smear their reputation

explanation.surface: An interrogation meant to disgrace a Gulf state.
explanation.definitionFit: Qatar is a small Gulf emirate on the Arabian Peninsula.

clue.text: Meditative utterance: "I see a Midwestern city"

parts.note: om is the syllable chanted in meditation
aha, the cry of realisation

explanation.surface: A meditator chants and suddenly spots a city in the heartland.
explanation.definitionFit: Omaha is the largest city in Nebraska, a state of the US Midwest.

clue.text: Stick around, primarily operating automobile in Sun Belt city

indicators.note: the stick goes around the next letters

parts.note: a baton is a stick, as a conductor or relay runner holds

indicators.note: primarily means first, so only the first letter of operating is used

parts.note: only its first letter is used
a car

explanation.surface: A baton is waved about while driving a car through a southern US city.
explanation.definitionFit: Boca Raton is a city in south Florida, part of the warm southern US region called the Sun Belt.

clue.text: Retch, cutting bliss short

indicators.note: cut short, the word for bliss loses its final letter

parts.note: heaven is a state of bliss

explanation.surface: Vomiting interrupts a moment of joy.
explanation.definitionFit: To heave is to gag or vomit, the sense of retching.

clue.text: Jumbled bronze pile that's been given to ten writers (counting carefully) whose names appear as complete answers in this puzzle

definitions.text: that's been given to ten writers (counting carefully) whose names appear as complete answers in this puzzle

indicators.note: jumbled letters are mixed up, so these are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A messy heap of bronze, the award a theme of writers has received.
explanation.walkthrough: BUCK, BELLOW, GRASS, LAXNESS, FRANCE, WHITE, SINGER, MISTRAL and QUASIMODO are laureates; the parenthesis warns that the count is a careful one.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nobel Prize in Literature is the award all the theme authors in this grid have received.
